lawyer:
Md. Rezaul Karim, Advocate-----For the Petitioner. 
Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate with Khondker Shamsul Hoque Reza, Advocate-----For the Opposite-Party No.2.
parties:
Elizabeth R. Das Wife of Bablu Robin D, Rozario ----- Petitioner
Vs
State and another ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. The short fact of the prosecution case is that Mrs. Elizabeth R. Das was married with the opposite party No.2, Bablu Robin D' Rozario on 26-10-1984. Their marriage was duly solemnized performing necessary ceremonies as per Christian Roman Catholic religion. The complainant Elizabeth R. Das and Bablu Robin D' Rozario were living together as husband and wife and they had been blessed with a son named as Brian D' Rozario. The accused Bablu Robin D' Rozario used to torture the complainant physically and mentally often and on. On 23-12-2006 he made the complainant bound to leave the house forcibly and threatened to remarry. Thereafter the complainant used to live in a separate rented house along with her son Brian D' Rozario but the accused did not take care of her and her son. On 29-8-2008 the accused got remarried with another woman, which is not permitted by Roman Catholic Christian Law of marriage. Thereafter the accused sent a notice of talak to the complainant on 03-9-2008. The complainant became astonished to receive the said notice of talak and tried to communicate with her husband but the opposite party No. 2 and her new wife Poly Das threatened over phone not to make any extreme over the matter in future. Hence the complainant lodged the instant General Diary with Tejgaon police Station. Upon receiving the said complaint the same was recorded as General Diary (GD) No. 375 dated 04-12-2008. 

 3. The Officer-in-Charge of Tejgaon Police Station investigated the case, the investigation officer after completion of investigation submitted a prosecution report before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka against the husband of the complainant under section 494 of the Penal Code. 

 4. Thereafter the case was transferred to the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate Court No.11 for trial, the trial was started with the framing of charge against the accused on 22-6-2009 under sections 494/109 of the Penal Code. 

 6. The defense case in brief is that the accused Bablu Robin D. Rozario did not get remarried. The complainant filed a suit for separation of their conjugal life and, as such, no offence under section 494 of the Penal Code has been committed by the accused. 

 9. Mr. Md. Rezaul Karim, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the appellate Court erred in law in failing to appreciate the evidence adduced by the PWs. He further submits that the trial Court was justified in pronouncing the Judgment, as it properly appreciated the evidence on record, particularly the evidence of PWs 2 and 3. He further submits that the second marriage of the opposite party No.2 was solemnized by a Protestant Pastor who has government license to solemnize protestant marriage only, he did not have any authority to solemnize any marriage of Roman Catholic believers. The appellate Court totally failed to appreciate this religious provision of Roman Catholic believers and, as such, he fell into an error and passed the impugned Judgment which has occasioned a failure of justice, as such the same is liable to be set aside. He further submits that although the papers regarding the second marriage of the accused with one Poly Das and the letters from the Tejgaon Church given by father TP Rebeiro, annexures-A and D, could not be produced before the trial Court or the appellate Court as those were not available at the relevant time, but by adducing oral evidence by the PWs, particularly by PW 2, the son of the accused, the second marriage of the accused has been proved. The Court of appeal below failed to appreciate this aspect of the case and, as such, he fell into an error in passing the impugned Judgment and Order which has caused miscarriage of justice and, as such, the same is liable to be set aside. He further submits that for a Roman Catholic believer a second marriage is absolutely prohibited by their personal law. As per provision of the Canon No. 1141 of Code of Canon Law, the personal law of Roman Catholics, a second marriage is absolutely prohibited for the Roman Catholics. Thus the opposite party No. 2 in violation of the provision of his personal law i.e. the Code of Canon Law, (Canon 1141) has remarried one Poly Das thus committed an offence which is punishable under section 494 of the Penal Code and, as such, the Judgment and Order of conviction and sentence of the trial Court was justified, the Court of appeal below failed to appreciate this provisions of law and thus fell into an error in acquitting the accused opposite party No. 2 which has caused miscarriage of justice to the petitioner. Mr. Md. Rezaul Karim also submits that as per Canon No. 1153, of Code of Canon Law, a Roman Catholic couple can be separated. When a spouse who causes grave spiritual or bodily harm to the other spouse or children or otherwise makes cohabitation too hard, he/she gives legitimate cause to the other to separate, but during existence of the first marriage there is no any scope for remarriage. The Court of appeal below found that the second marriage could not be proved by adducing any papers from the Church. In this context Mr. Md. Rezaul Karim submits that since 2nd marriage can not be solemnized by a Roman Catholic Church as per the Code of Canon Law of Roman Catholics no Church of Roman Catholic will solemnize such kind of marriage. Thus the papers from any Roman Catholic Church could not be obtained, but he also submits that the second marriage was solemnized by one Jewel Biswas a Protestant Pastor, Protestants are also believer of Christianity, but they belong a separate group, their priests and Churches are quite different. Solemnization of marriage by a different priest other than the priest of Roman Catholics is not permissible in the law, but nevertheless a marriage has been solemnized by a priest of different group, which is a punishable offence under section 494 of the Penal Code. The Judge in the Court of appeal below failed to consider this aspect of the case and, as such, he fell into an error which has caused miscarriage of justice. Finally, Mr. Md. Rezaul Karim prays for making the Rule absolute, setting aside the Judgment and Order passed by the lower appellate Court. 

 10. On the other hand Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 2 along with Mr. Khondker Shamsul Hoque Reza, learned advocate submits that since the marriage has not been proved by adducing any paper or by examining any priest from the Church the Court of appeal below has rightly acquitted the opposite party No. 2 and set aside the Judgment and Order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Magistrate in non GR Case No. 217 of 2009 arising out of non FIR Case No. 19 dated 17-1-2009. He further submits that section 494 of the Penal Code does not attract in this case, because to attract section 494 of the Penal Code second marriage must be proved. Since the marriage of the opposite party No. 2 has not been solemnized by any priest of Roman Catholic Church, in the eye of law there is no any existence of second marriage in this case. He submits that if the accused-opposite party No. 2 had lived with any woman, it may be a social offence or offence under different section of the Penal Code or any other law, but in no way it can be said that he has married the lady with whom he lived, unless the marriage is solemnized in due course. Thus section 494 of the Penal Code in no way attracts to convict the opposite party No. 2. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan further submits that the allegation made by the complainant is not supported by any written document, the prosecution miserably failed to produce any document in respect of their allegation of second marriage before the Courts below. He also submits that this Court sitting in a revisional jurisdiction cannot see the papers which have been submitted before this Court, annexing with the application. He further submits that the PW 1 in her deposition stated that she came to know about remarriage of her husband from her relatives, but in her cross-examination she deposed that the marriage was solemnized by one Jewel Biswas a Protestant Pastor, but this Jewel Biswas did not come to the Court to support the statement of the PW 1 or the case of the complainant. More so she had failed to produce any document of marriage, which has disproved the allegation of second marriage. Mr. Khurshid Alam Khan further submits that in Christianity every marriage is registered by the Church, but in this case the documents, which have been produced by the prosecution was not issued from any Church, which casts a serious doubt about the prosecution case. Moreover, the PW 2 himself stated that the marriage was solemnized in a Chinese restaurant, instead of a Church, which proves that in the eye of law there was no marriage and thus the opposite party No. 2 in no way can be charged for second marriage. Thus the Court of appeal below has rightly acquitted him from the charge brought against him and has set aside the Judgment and Order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Magistrate in the trial Court. He further submits that essential ceremonies necessary to constitute a second marriage were not performed and, as such, there was no any second marriage at all and, as such, the case does not come within the ambit of section 494 of the Penal Code. Hence the instant Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 11. I have gone through the revisional application along with the annexures filed by the petitioner and considered the submissions of the learned advocate of both sides. I have also gone through the provision of laws. It is admitted that the petitioner was married to the opposite party No. 2 on 26-10-1984 and their marriage was duly solemnized performing necessary ceremonies as per Christian religion (Roman Catholic). The complainant and the opposite party No. 2 both are believers of Christianity, Roman Catholic group, at their wedlock a son namely Brian D. Rozario was born on 08-9-1986 and after a lapse of about 24 years a dispute arose between husband and wife. The wife's allegation is that her husband used to torture her and her son and he has taken a second wife. It is observed by this Court that in both the Judgments it has been mentioned that without the permission of the first wife the opposite party No. 2 took a second wife. Both the Judges in the Courts below are believers of Islam, perhaps the provision of Muslim Family Laws Ordinance worked at the back of their minds thus both the Courts below mentioned that the opposite party No. 2, took a 2nd wife without permission of his 1st wife. In Canon 1141 of the Code of Canon Law, it has been 'clearly mentioned that "A marriage which is ratified and consummated cannot be dissolved by any human power or by any cause other than death" which proves that the Roman Catholic believers cannot divorce each other, they can live separately, but there is no provision for remarriage and there is no any provision to provide any permission to remarry which is available in Muslim Family Laws Ordinance. The Courts below from their misconception hold that, without permission of the first wife the accused-opposite party No. 2 took his second wife. The Court of appeal below after going through the Judgment of the trial Court has come to a decision that the second marriage has not been proved by any tangible evidence and thus he set aside the Judgment of the trial Court. 

 14. In her cross-examination this witness stated that her husband took a 2nd wife without her consent. She further stated that the place where the second marriage was solemnized, it was mentioned in the GD Entry. She further stated that she submitted the papers regarding the second marriage of her husband to the investigation officer. She also stated that she gave the certificate of the second marriage of her husband and the photograph of the new bride and the bridegroom to the investigation officer. She denied the suggestion that she did not hand over any papers to the investigating officer. In her cross-examination she also stated that one Jewel Biswas solemnized the second marriage. She further stated that she could not say whether Jewel Biswas was cited as witness. Subsequently, she said he is not a witness of this case. She denied the suggestion that the opposite party No. 2 did not take a second wife, she emphatically stated that accused Bablu married Poly Das and she is pregnant. She further stated that on 29-8-2008 the second marriage was solemnized and she lodged GD Entry on 05-12-2008 and she also filed a civil suit on 30-11-2008 demanding separation. 

 Which clearly proves that the PW 3 was present in the marriage ceremony of opposite party No.2 and he talked with the PW 2 regarding the programme held in the Chinese restaurant. The appellate Court has also observed that "no papers were supplied from the Church, if the marriage would have been solemnized in a Church the papers would have been supplied in a letter head with seal of the Church, but in this case those are absent." The learned Judge in the Court of appeal below failed to appreciate that, this is the case of the complainant that the second marriage was not solemnized in any Roman Catholic Church, because there was no scope as per law to solemnize any second marriage in a Roman Catholic Church. The alleged marriage was administered by one Jewel Biswas, who was the Protestant Pastor at the relevant time. From the evidence of P Ws 1,2 and 3 it appears to me that they categorically stated about the second marriage of the opposite party No.2 and they corroborated one another in respect of solemnization of the second marriage and the social programme ("Bou Bhat") held in Yang Tune Chinese Restaurant. The programme of Yang Tune Chinese Restaurant was a social programme, in pursuant to the marriage solemnized and administered by one Jewel Biswas. In support of ' this marriage the petitioner has submitted some papers before this Court annexing those with this revisional application. Annexure-A is a certificate dated 13-11-2007 given by father TP Rebeiro, Chancellor, Archdiocese of Dhaka, Parish Priest, Holy Rosary Church, Tejgaon. By this certificate he described the sufferings of the petitioner in his family life. Annexure-A(1) is another certificate dated 25-10-2008 issued from the same Church of Tejgaon where it has been written that "now we hear that Bablu Robin married some Poly Das and he is living with her." Annexure-A(2) is a certificate given by one Anowar-uz-zaman, Commissioner of Ward No. 40, Dhaka City Corporation. In his certificate he also wrote that "Mr. Bablu Robin D' Rozario has been living with one Poly Das together." Annexure-D is a page of marriage registrar's book in which it has been mentioned that "Bablu Rabin D. Rozario married one Poly Das." It is a certificate by which it has been proved that Robin D' Rozario married Poly Das. The question is whether these papers can be looked into at this stage. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, learned advocate for the opposite party No.2 submits that these papers should have been submitted before the trial Court and without having any exhibit mark these papers for the first time have been placed before this Court, sitting in a revisional jurisdiction this Court does not have any jurisdiction to look into these papers. On the other hand Mr. Md. Rezaul Karim, learned advocate submits that since by the oral evidence it has been proved that the opposite party No.2 has already taken a second wife, through a marriage solemnized by one Protestant Pastor. Only this statement has been substantiated by filing these papers in support of the oral evidence adduced by the prosecution witnesses before this Court. He also added that all those papers were submitted to the concerned Court along with the prosecution report. This Court is competent enough to look into these documents. In this regard Mr. Rezaul Karim refers the case of Shafiqur Rahman vs Nurul Islam Chowdhury reported in 35 DLR (AD) 127, in this decision Their Lordships held that— 

 "The object of revisional jurisdiction is to confer upon superior criminal Courts a kind of paternal or supervisory jurisdiction in order to correct miscarriage of justice arising from misconception of law, irregularity of procedure, neglect of proper precautions, or apparent harshness of treatment which has resulted in some injury to public interest or undue hardship to individual. This is a part of the observations made by the Law Reform Commission set up by the Government of Pakistan in 1967." Their Lordships also held that— 

 "No hard and fast limitation should be placed on the exercise of the High Court's powers of superintendence over the proceedings in inferior Courts; and that there is no species of injustice which the High Court would be powerless to correct under the Chapter where its interference is called for. The High Court has plenary powers of interference under the Chapter, where it is needed to correct injustice. It has been held that under section 439 very wide powers of revision were intended to be conferred on the High Court. The meaning of that section is that in any case to which sections 435 or 438 is applicable, the High Court can with reference to any particular order (whether appealable or not) exercise all or any of the powers which under section 423 an appellate Court could exercise, if that order happened to be one open to appeal; and it was not intended by the Legislature that the High Court's powers of revision were to be limited merely to orders from which appeal would lie. Obviously the main idea is that the High Court should be in a position to rectify cases of injustice or illegality when the person affected is unable to appeal." 

 22. From the above decision it is very clear that the High Court Division sitting in revisional jurisdiction is amply empowered to see whether the Courts below has done any neglect in taking proper precautions and also the High Court Division is in a position to rectify the causes of injustice and illegality of the Courts below. In this case, I find that the Court of appeal below totally ignored the evidence of PW 2, the son of the opposite party No. 2 and the evidence of PW 3 the friend of PW 2 and also misquoted their evidence in his Judgment. Furthermore, the papers which have been submitted to this Court are nothing new, these papers have been submitted only in support of evidence adduced by the PWs. These papers were also supplied to the investigation officer, the investigation officer in his deposition stated that those papers were submitted before the trial Court. Although these papers were not marked as exhibit, but still in my opinion sitting in a revisional jurisdiction this Court can see these papers for ensuring justice as those have been submitted in support of the evidence adduced by the PWs 1 to 4. 

 23. The contention of Mr. Khurshid Alam Khan is that, in the eye of law the 2nd marriage was not solemnized in due course. I am of the view that, even if factually the marriage was solemnized by the Protestant Pastor which is not a legal marriage still section 494 can be invoked, because no matter whether or not marriage was solemnized under a proper procedure, but since one priest of a particular group has administered the marriage it has some social value. Society knows that opposite party No. 2 has married Poly Das as his second wife. The trial Court rightly came to a decision that the opposite party No. 2 married Poly Das as his 2nd wife. In absence of any formal proof the Court has to form an opinion as to relationship of one person to another, the opinion expressed by conduct, as to the existence of such relationship, if any person who as a member of family or otherwise has spectral means of knowledge on the subject is relevant fact. In this case the son of the opposite party No. 2 by giving evidence in the Court has proved the offence which is punishable under section 494 of the Penal Code. 

 "Whoever, having a husband or wife living, marries in any case in which such marriage is void by reason of its taking place during the life of such husband or wife, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine" 

 27. In the absence of formal proof of a valid marriage, a marriage can be presumed by evidence of conduct and reputation. Continual co-habitation between a man and a woman as husband and wife an inference can be drawn that they are married couple. In this case, I am of the view that the PWs 1 to 4 corroborating one another have been able to prove that the opposite party No.2 and Poly Das lived together and Poly Das became pregnant by the opposite party No.2 which proves their marriage and, as such, the Judgment and Order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court was justified. 

 28. The lower appellate Court failed to appreciate the evidence adduced by the PWs and without proper discussion of those evidence he fell into an error and passed the impugned Judgment setting aside the Judgment and Order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Magistrate and acquitted the appellant. Which has caused miscarriage of justice.
